title: Fix step_holiday time zone conversion
description:
## Summary
Fix the time-zone conversion used by `step_holiday()` for POSIXct inputs.

## Thanks to maintainers
Thanks to Emil Hvitfeldt for the clear reproducer and suggested fix, and to the recipes maintainers for maintaining the package.

## Issue or motivation
Addresses #1564: timestamps near local midnight could receive the wrong holiday indicator.

## Root cause
`as.Date()` converts POSIXct values through UTC before dropping the time, which can shift the calendar date away from the timestamp's local date.

## Change
Use `lubridate::as_date()` in `get_holiday_features()` and add a regression test for a Pacific-time New Year's Day timestamp.

## Tests
- Focused holiday tests and full `devtools::test()` passed. Fourteen optional `RcppML` tests were skipped; the full test run reported one macOS locale warning because `fr_FR.UTF8` is unavailable.
- `R CMD build --no-manual`, `R CMD check --no-manual`, and `R CMD check --as-cran --no-manual` passed. As-cran reported one development-version NOTE; remote URL and system-clock probes were disabled after network errors.
- Air formatting, the covr workflow command (96.13% coverage), and the pkgdown site build passed.
- GitHub Actions `format-suggest` failed at fork checkout before running Air; the R-CMD-check, hard-check, coverage, and pkgdown workflows are `action_required`. Their local equivalents above passed.

## Scope
Date inputs and other recipe steps are unchanged.

title: Add stop_at argument to bake()
description:
Closes #1551.

Adds a `stop_at` argument to `bake()` so users can see the data as it exists partway through a prepped recipe, which is handy for visual diagnostics.

```r
rec <- recipe(cyl ~ ., mtcars) |>
  step_center(all_predictors()) |>
  step_pca(all_predictors(), num_comp = 2) |>
  prep()

bake(rec, mtcars, stop_at = 1)              # by step number
bake(rec, mtcars, stop_at = "center_zo5Cx") # by step id
```

Details:

* `stop_at` sits after `...`, so it is named-only and can't be confused with tidyselect terms. The `bake()` generic is `function(object, ...)`, so it needed no change. Default `NULL` keeps the current behavior.
* Steps with `skip = TRUE` keep their existing semantics and still count toward the numbering, so numbers line up with `tidy(rec)`.
* `stop_at` errors with `new_data = NULL`. That path returns `object$template`, the fully processed training set, and `prep()` does not retain the raw training data, so intermediate stages can't be reconstructed. The message points users at passing the training data to `new_data`.
* The post-loop column selection normally uses `last_term_info`, which describes the data after *all* steps and so is wrong for a partial bake. Deriving the info from the intermediate data alone wasn't enough: roles for derived columns were lost, and `all_numeric_predictors()` selected nothing after `step_pca()`. Instead `update_term_info()` tracks the term info as each step is applied, mirroring the logic in `prep()`. It only runs when `stop_at` is supplied, so the default path is unaffected.

Tests cover step numbers, step ids, selectors, `composition = "dgCMatrix"`, a mid-recipe `skip = TRUE` step, and snapshot errors for out-of-range numbers, non-whole numbers, unknown ids, wrong types, length > 1, `new_data = NULL`, and a recipe with no steps.

`devtools::check()` is clean: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes.

title: Allow step_count() and step_regex() to select multiple columns
description:
Both steps were limited to a single variable, so `step_regex(description, rows)` errored in the constructor and a selector like `all_string_predictors()` that happened to resolve to several columns died later with an opaque tibble subscript error. title: Speed up last_term_info bookkeeping in prep()
description:
Profiling `prep()` on a 20,000-column recipe showed that building `last_term_info` accounted for 44% of the total time. `running_info` has one row per column per step, so the grouped `summarise()` over it was by far the most expensive part of `prep()`. This computes the same thing with a sort and a group lookup, cutting `prep()` roughly in half on wide recipes (1.49s to 1.15s at 20,000 columns, 2.41s to 1.62s at 30,000).

The result is `identical()` to the previous output, including the grouping on `variable`, which downstream code relies on. I checked that across recipes with added columns, removed columns, `skip = TRUE`, extra roles, and no steps at all.

One caveat on reading the numbers: the timings above are measured on top of the `bake()` fixes in #1556 and #1558. On main the quadratic `bake()` cost dominates `prep()` entirely (61s at 20,000 columns), so this change looks like noise there. It stands alone and doesn't depend on those PRs, but it is only worth much once they land.

Refs #1543.

title: Combine generated columns once per step instead of once per column
description:
Six steps that add new columns called `vctrs::vec_cbind()` inside their loop over the selected columns, which copies the whole data set on every iteration and makes `bake()` quadratic in the number of columns. They now accumulate the generated columns and combine once, matching what `step_spline_*()`, `step_poly*()`, `step_date()`, and `step_indicate_na()` already do. Baking 4,000 factor columns through `step_dummy()` drops from 2.66s to 0.95s, and the scaling goes from roughly tripling per doubling of width to roughly doubling, so the gap keeps widening beyond that.

This is a different problem from the one in #1556 and shares no code with it, so the two are independent. `step_dummy()` needed the most care: it re-levels the incoming factors in place, and those re-levelled columns are visible in the output when `keep_original_cols = TRUE`, so that write-back now happens in bulk after the loop.

Refs #1543.

## Test plan

Because `new_data` no longer grows inside these loops, `check_name()` no longer sees previously generated columns. Collisions with existing columns are still caught the same way, and `step_dummy()` gained an explicit check for collisions between generated names, which is reachable with a custom `naming` function:

```r
d <- data.frame(a = factor(c("x", "y")), b = factor(c("p", "q")))
same <- function(var, lvl, ordinal = FALSE, sep = NULL) "dup"
recipes::prep(recipes::step_dummy(recipes::recipe(~., d), a, b, naming = same))
#> Error: Name collision occurred. The following variable names already exist: `dup`
```

Worth confirming that still errors with the recipes message rather than a raw vctrs one.

title: Use recipes_map_cols() in the remaining in-place steps
description:
Converts the rest of the steps that transform columns in place, the ones whose per-column work needs more context than a scalar parameter: the factor level steps, the model-based imputation steps, and `step_window()`. Baking 8,000 factor columns through `step_other()` drops from 5.14s to 1.26s and through `step_novel()` from 7.86s to 3.28s. The two check functions don't assign anything, so they just subset their columns once instead of looking each one up by name.

`step_impute_bag()`, `step_impute_knn()`, and `step_impute_linear()` each kept an `old_data <- new_data` copy so that predictors were read from unimputed data. Since the data is no longer modified while mapping, that copy is gone and the predictors are read from `new_data` directly.

Targets #1556 rather than main, since it builds on `recipes_map_cols()`. Refs #1543.

title: Speed up bake() for data with many columns
description:
Steps that transformed columns in place did so by assigning to `new_data[[col_name]]` inside a loop, which is quadratic in the number of columns and made recipes unusable on wide data: the reprex in #1543 took over four minutes to prep and bake 60,000 predictors. Two separate costs stack up, the per-column tibble restore and the linear name lookup on every iteration, so this adds a `recipes_map_cols()` helper that fixes both and converts the 27 steps that had the pattern. The same reprex now runs in about five seconds and scales linearly.

`recipes_map_cols()` is exported for extension packages, following the same `@keywords internal` convention as `check_new_data()` and `remove_original_cols()`. It passes the column's position rather than only its name, since looking up a per-column parameter by name is half of what made the original loop slow.

Fixes #1543.

## Test plan

Two message regressions were caught by existing snapshots and fixed rather than accepted, so it's worth confirming no snapshot churn:

```r
Rscript -e "devtools::test()"
```

`step_integer()` is still slow on wide data (~23s to bake 20,000 columns), but that cost is linear and comes from the per-column `dplyr::full_join()` in `map_key_to_int()`, unrelated to the quadratic issue fixed here. Left for a follow-up.

title: Fix imputation steps erroring on data with survival outcomes
description:
Using `step_impute_bag()`, `step_impute_knn()`, or `step_impute_linear()` on data with a `Surv()` outcome failed with "C stack usage is too close to the limit", because their `bake()` methods scanned the whole of `new_data` for missing values and `vctrs::vec_detect_complete()` recurses infinitely on a `Surv` column. Narrowing that early-exit check to just the columns being imputed fixes it, and is more correct anyway: missingness in an untouched outcome column has no bearing on whether the step has work to do.

Fixes #1542.

title: Add tidy-add-step-argument skill
description:
Converts the "adding an argument to an existing step" checklist from `vignettes/articles/checklists.Rmd` into a Claude skill, alongside the existing `tidy-argument-checking` and `tidy-deprecate-function` skills. Threading a new argument through the constructor, `step_*_new()`, and `prep()` is easy to get subtly wrong, and the failure mode is a step that silently ignores the argument or an old saved recipe that breaks, so it is worth having the procedure to hand while working rather than only when pasted into an issue.

The vignette stays as the human-facing version to copy into a GitHub issue. Part of #1550; this covers recipes only, and copying the skill to the extension packages is left for a follow-up.

title: Fix unrelated R-CMD-check failures on old R and macOS
description:
R-CMD-check is currently red on `main`-based branches for two reasons, neither related to package code. Both showed up on #1552, which only touches `bake()`.

**`ubuntu-latest (oldrel-3)`, `ubuntu-latest (oldrel-4)`, `windows-latest (oldrel-4)`** fail in `setup-r-dependencies`, before the package is even built:

```
! Could not solve package dependencies:
* deps::.: Can't install dependency mixOmics
* mixOmics: Can't find package called mixOmics.
```

The Bioconductor repos for those R versions now 404 (`bioconductor.posit.co/packages/3.18/...`), so pak can't resolve the suggested mixOmics package (a Suggests since #1544). This ignores mixOmics below R 4.4.0, exactly as igraph is already handled on the same line. Everything that uses it (`step_pls()` and friends) is guarded by `skip_if_not_installed("mixOmics")`, so the older jobs just skip those tests.

**`macos-latest (release)`** fails installing recipes:

```
unable to load shared object '.../gower/libs/gower.so':
  symbol not found in flat namespace '___kmpc_barrier'
```

`___kmpc_barrier` is an OpenMP runtime symbol. The job installs the P3M binary (`packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest/bin/macosx/sonoma-arm64/contrib/4.6/gower_1.0.2.tgz`), which is built with OpenMP, but the runner has no libomp available for the flat-namespace lookup. CRAN's own macOS binaries are built without OpenMP, so this turns `use-public-rspm` off for the macOS job only; the other jobs are unaffected.

The macOS half is a hypothesis I can't verify locally, so it's worth watching this PR's own macOS job before merging. The mixOmics half is well understood.

docs: clarify how variables are filtered out in step_corr()
description:
I was curious on how step_corr() was filtering out variables and found one answer here by Max https://forum.posit.co/t/how-does-step-corr-pick-which-variable-to-keep/46496/3

> In general, the filter tries to prioritize predictors for removal based on the global affect on the overall correlation structure. If you had two identical predictors, there is no real rule on which one to retain (it probably gets rid of the first one or something like that).

Thought I'd add some of the prose into the `help(step_corr)` page in this commit/PR so others know a little bit about how it works.

I was also curious about how it _actually_ chooses, and went into the code itself https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/blob/602dd48ecfe95535457ee422d856054a45833df4/R/corr.R#L248C1-L257C36:

```r
    averageCorr <- colMeans(abs(x))
    averageCorr <- as.numeric(as.factor(averageCorr))
    x[lower.tri(x, diag = TRUE)] <- NA
    combsAboveCutoff <- which(abs(x) > cutoff)

    colsToCheck <- ceiling(combsAboveCutoff / nrow(x))
    rowsToCheck <- combsAboveCutoff %% nrow(x)

    colsToDiscard <- averageCorr[colsToCheck] > averageCorr[rowsToCheck]
    rowsToDiscard <- !colsToDiscard
```

It took a bit to figure out that it really is kind of random (it is based on the "meaningless" numeric value assigned to levels of factors). I didn't want to add all the details of this matrix filtering in the help documentation, so I left code comments in there in case anyone else wants to read and understand. Feel free to suggest remove these comments if it feels too unnecessary.

Thanks!

title: add `.recipes_estimate_sparsity()`
description:
To close #1397

I think i found a fairly elegant solution. it adds another S3 method, one with methods for the whole recipe, and for individual steps. This way steps that produce sparsity can return how much sparsity they produce.

It uses the newly added `sparsity()` function from {sparsevctrs} to estimate an initial sparsity of the input-data. Downsampling to 1000 rows for performance reasons.

Then each step that will produce sparse predictors will via their S3 method return how many columns and how sparse, they expect to return. This is used to update the estimate and repeated for each input/step.

the it obviously over estimates for `recipe() |> step_other(col) |> step_dummy(col)`, but it is the best we can do IMO with unprepped recipes. An user still have the option to overwrite anyways.

It is quite a bit faster than prepping the recipe. And from profiling the most significant time comes from `sparsevctrs::sparsity()`, which has room for improvement if needed.

``` r
library(recipes)
library(modeldata)

rec_sparse <- recipe(~., ames) |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal())

rec_sparse_no <- recipe(~., ames) |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal(), sparse = "no")

rec_dense_0 <- recipe(~., ames)

rec_dense_10 <- recipe(~., ames) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric())

bench::mark(
  check = FALSE,
  prep_sparse = prep(rec_sparse),
  est_sparse = .recipes_estimate_sparsity(rec_sparse),
  est_sparse_no = .recipes_estimate_sparsity(rec_sparse_no),
  est_dense_0 = .recipes_estimate_sparsity(rec_dense_0),
  est_dense_10 = .recipes_estimate_sparsity(rec_dense_10)
)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 6
#>   expression         min   median `itr/sec` mem_alloc `gc/sec`
#>   <bch:expr>    <bch:tm> <bch:tm>     <dbl> <bch:byt>    <dbl>
#> 1 prep_sparse     64.8ms   67.3ms      13.3    56.8MB     28.5
#> 2 est_sparse     916.6µs  978.3µs     960.    790.7KB     18.0
#> 3 est_sparse_no  305.4µs  335.9µs    2692.      507KB     46.0
#> 4 est_dense_0    302.5µs  335.4µs    2713.      507KB     46.0
#> 5 est_dense_10   305.3µs  340.6µs    2387.      507KB     36.0
```

And it is decently good for recipes it understand.

```r
.recipes_estimate_sparsity(rec_sparse)
#> [1] 0.7993268
rec_sparse |> prep() |> bake(NULL) |> sparsevctrs::sparsity()
#> [1] 0.7953081
```

title: fix bug in step_ns where knots didn't get passed through
description:
to close #1297 and close https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/issues/1050.

The main problem was that `knots` wasn't passed through if it was set in `options` argument

``` r
library(recipes)
d <- tibble(x = seq(-2, 2, 0.01))

rec_res <- recipe(~., data = d) %>% 
  step_ns(x, options = list(knots = seq(-1, 1, 0.125), 
                            Boundary.knots = c(-1.5, 1.5))) %>% 
  prep() %>% 
  bake(new_data = d)

# -1 in `model.matrix()` to avoid intercept
mm_res <- model.matrix(~splines::ns(x, 
                          knots = seq(-1, 1, 0.125), 
                          Boundary.knots = c(-1.5, 1.5)) - 1, data = d)

attr(mm_res, "assign") <- NULL

identical(
  rec_res,
  setNames(as_tibble(mm_res), names(rec_res))
)
#> [1] TRUE
```

title: Add ptype information to recipes
description:
This looks at how we could add ptype information to the recipe.

I think the best plan of action is to take a ptype slice of the entire dataset passed to `recipe()` and then have helper functions to pull out the needed information.

Because the `ptype` information that the user/functions need will depend:

- ptype checking for the data passed to `prep()` should match the data passed to `recipe()`
- ptype checking for for data passed to `bake()` shouldn't match against outcome roles
- In essence, everything will depend on the roles, and work with `update_role_requirements()`

### Revdepcheck

I ran revdepcheck on the change to add a `ptype` field to the recipe object and it came back with no issues

title: Adds support for `tbl_lazy()` to `recipe()`
description:
This is the first PR that begins extending `recipes` into remote tables.  The idea is to setup the infrastructure in the main functions, as well as to centralize support for `tbl_lazy` objects.  These objects are used by `dplyr` on database connectivity packages, as well as `sparklyr`.  Highlights:

- It modifies the `recipe.data.frame()` function to enable it to accept non-data.frame objects.  Opted for this approach because of the current, and future, argument validation that happen inside this function.  The changes were minimal, so I figured it would be best to make them in this function, instead of copying the argument validation into another method
- Adds a `recipe.tbl_lazy()` method
- Renames `get_type()` to `recipes_translate_types()` and exports it.  This will allow other packages to pass custom type translation, such as `sparklyr`.
- Adds a `recipes_translate_types.tbl_lazy()` method. It will be the default translation for remote tables.  It collects the top 10 rows into memory, in order for the original `get_type()` code to determine types.  Because it is exported, this behavior can be customized based on the remote connection.  In the example below, I created a custom `tbl_spark` method for it. It uses the metadata about the field types already within the table object, so there is no need to collect the top 10.  I expect this function will be in `sparklyr` in a future release
-   Adds an un-exported `select_variables` method.  Its purpose is to add the ability to switch between using `tidyeval_eval_select()` for `data.frames` , and other methods to extract the selected variables if the object is not a `data.frame`. 
-  Added `select_variables.tbl_lazy()`.  Which emulates the output from the original `tidyeval::eval_select()`.  Today, it ignores the `allow_rename` argument. 

The resulting `recipe` object is identical as if was created using a local R `data.frame` with one exception.  The `template` item will not be a `data.frame` but a whatever the remote table is being used.  This is not an issue until a function such as `prep` is attempted.  This will be addressed in a subsequent PR. 

``` r
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(sparklyr))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(recipes))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(DBI))

# ----- Example using a database connection

con <- dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), dbname = ":memory:")

tbl_mtcars <- copy_to(con, mtcars)

remote_r <- recipe(tbl_mtcars) %>%
  step_select(mpg, am) %>%
  step_filter(am == 1)


remote_r
#> Recipe
#> 
#> Inputs:
#> 
#>   11 variables (no declared roles)
#> 
#> Operations:
#> 
#> Variables selected mpg, am
#> Row filtering using am == 1

# ----- Example using a Spark connection

sc <- spark_connect("local")

spark_mtcars <- copy_to(sc, mtcars)


# Created a custom type translation method using the new recipes_translate_types() function
recipes_translate_types.tbl_spark <- function(x) {
  type_map <- c(
    BooleanType = "logical",
    ByteType = "numeric",
    ShortType = "numeric",
    IntegerType = "numeric",
    FloatType = "numeric",
    DoubleType = "numeric",
    LongType = "numeric",
    StringType = "nominal",
    BinaryType = "nominal",
    TimestampType = "date",
    DateType = "date"
  )

  table_schema <- sdf_schema(x)

  purrr::map_dfr(table_schema, ~ {
    match_type <- names(type_map) == .x$type
    new_type <- type_map[match_type]
    tibble(variable = .x$name, type = new_type)
  })
}

spark_r <- recipe(spark_mtcars) %>%
  step_select(mpg, am) %>%
  step_filter(am == 1)

spark_r
#> Recipe
#> 
#> Inputs:
#> 
#>   11 variables (no declared roles)
#> 
#> Operations:
#> 
#> Variables selected mpg, am
#> Row filtering using am == 1

spark_disconnect(sc)

local_r <- recipe(mtcars) %>%
  step_select(mpg, am) %>%
  step_filter(am == 1)


local_r
#> Recipe
#> 
#> Inputs:
#> 
#>   11 variables (no declared roles)
#> 
#> Operations:
#> 
#> Variables selected mpg, am
#> Row filtering using am == 1
```

title: fix mistake in documented default value of keep_original_cols
description:
to close https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/issues/1276 and close https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/issues/1267

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(recipes)

steps <- ls(getNamespace("recipes")) |>
  stringr::str_subset("^step_") |>
  stringr::str_subset("_new$", negate = TRUE)


get_arg <- function(x) {
  res <- getFromNamespace(x, getNamespace("recipes"))
  res <- formals(res)
  res$keep_original_cols
}

get_doc <- function(x) {
  readLines(paste0("man/", x, ".Rd")) |>
    paste(collapse = " ") |>
    str_extract("\\item\\{keep_original_cols\\}\\{.*?\\item") |>
    str_remove("\\item\\{keep_original_cols\\}\\{") |>
    str_remove("\\} *\\\\item") |>
    str_remove(".*\\{") |>
    str_remove("\\}.*") |>
    as.logical()
}

tibble(
  name = steps
) |>
  mutate(default = purrr::map(steps, get_arg)) |>
  filter(lengths(default) > 0) |>
  mutate(default = unlist(default)) |>
  mutate(doc = map_lgl(name, get_doc)) |>
  filter(default != doc)

#> # A tibble: 10 × 3
#> name                      default doc  
#> <chr>                     <lgl>   <lgl>
#> 1 step_classdist          TRUE    FALSE
#> 2 step_classdist_shrunken TRUE    FALSE
```

title: use cli for all recipe.R functions
description:
ref: https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/issues/1237

This PR is a little longer, but felt right in the moment. It converts to {cli} in

- `recipe()`
- `prep()`
- `bake()`
- `juice()`

it also does a big improvement, that is best shown in the commit https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/commit/1c3e0a1b8c17b61e8a14a0e5455ccd4a187e6bfb, where the checking for `tune()` is now done all at once, instead of one step at a time.

# This PR

``` r
library(recipes)
library(hardhat)

recipe(~., data = mtcars) |>
  step_pca(all_predictors(), threshold = tune()) |>
  step_kpca(all_predictors(), num_comp = tune()) |>
  step_bs(all_predictors(), deg_free = tune()) |>
  prep()
#> Error in `prep()`:
#> ✖ You cannot `prep()` a tuneable recipe.
#> ℹ The following steps has `tune()`:
#> • step_pca: `threshold`
#> • step_kpca: `num_comp`
#> • step_bs: `deg_free`
```

# Before

``` r
library(recipes)
library(hardhat)

recipe(~., data = mtcars) |>
  step_pca(all_predictors(), threshold = tune()) |>
  step_kpca(all_predictors(), num_comp = tune()) |>
  step_bs(all_predictors(), deg_free = tune()) |>
  prep()
#> Error in `prep()`:
#> ! You cannot `prep()` a tuneable recipe. Argument(s) with `tune()`: 'threshold'. Do you want to use a tuning function such as `tune_grid()`?
```

spline2_apply speed and memory. To close #1200

``` r
library(recipes)

n <- 20000000

deg_free <- 8

# b-spline
s <- bSpline(x, deg_free = deg_free)

bench::mark(
  apply(s, 2, I),
  {attributes(s) <- list(dim = dim(s), dimnames = dimnames(s));s},
  iterations = 1
)
```

title: Loop cleaning
description:
This is quite a big PR.

it tries to give a more strieght forward unified approach to how to do things in `bake_step_*()` functions.

The gist of this, is that for many cases, we want to have the functions use the following structure

```r
for (col_name in col_names) {
  do something with  new_data[[col_name]]
}
```

It also has the benefit that the column names `col_names` are only extracted once, so we will gain a little speed and consistency that way.

Getting rid of `map()` inside `bake_step_*()` functions is also beneficial since they mess up the error handling/passing we are trying to use.

# Todo

The following steps needs these changes but for various reason didn't get done now. I'm planning on addressing these in separate PRs first.

- [x] `step_window()` https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/pull/1172
    - is a 1 to many step, but doens’t act like it
- [x] `step_regex()` https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/pull/1169
    - similar to step_dummy(), missing keep_orginal_cols()
- [x] `step_ratio()` https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/pull/1173
    - doesn’t feel right
- [x] `step_profile()` https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/pull/1177
    - also feels weird
- [x] `step_ns()` https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/pull/1178
    - more work
- [x] `step_lag()` https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/pull/1179
    - is a 1 to many step, but doesn’t act like it
- [x] `step_impute_linear()`, `step_impute_knn()`, `step_impute_bag()` https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/pull/1184
    - missing lots of things. such as recipes_eval_select()
- [x] `step_depth()` https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/pull/1180
    - missing check_new_data()
- [x] `step_count() ` https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/pull/1169
    - is similar to step_regex()
- [x] `step_classdist()` https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/pull/1183
    - similar to step_dummy() missing keep_orginal_cols()
- [x] `step_bs()` https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/pull/1178
    - more work
- [x] `step_dummy()` https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/pull/1182

## example benchmark

```r
old <- function(new_data, object) {
  if (length(object$columns) > 0) {
    for (i in seq_along(object$columns)) {
      new_data[, object$columns[i]] <-
        sample(getElement(new_data, object$columns[i]))
    }
  }
  new_data
}

new <- function(new_data, object) {
  col_names <- object$columns
  for (col_name in col_names) {
    new_data[[col_name]] <- sample(new_data[[col_name]])
  }
  new_data
}

object <- list(columns = colnames(mtcars))

bench::mark(
  check = FALSE,
  old(mtcars, object),
  new(mtcars, object)
)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   expression               min   median `itr/sec` mem_alloc `gc/sec`
#>   <bch:expr>          <bch:tm> <bch:tm>     <dbl> <bch:byt>    <dbl>
#> 1 old(mtcars, object)  158.5µs    167µs     5772.    4.34MB     41.4
#> 2 new(mtcars, object)   97.2µs    104µs     9231.  169.21KB     41.9
```

There are some times where we have a long `if ()` statement, when only trigger sometimes. I switched these over to adopt an early exit strategy. Which we use in other places, such as in `step_count()`

https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/blob/13849d2a16d300eb66d5b9b40e53dc771b5e4e6a/R/count.R#L141-L146

For this refactor, it is important to remember the rule `!(A and B)` is the same as `!A or !B`.

This PR looks like there are more changes then there actually is. The majority of the changes are indentation changes

title: Add recipes_get_features() functions
description:
This PR is a WIP work to close https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/issues/1137.

If we end up doing this it will be a BIG PR, that we have to be very careful off not to break anything backwards.

As demo to describe the problem, see below. This recipe has two steps `step_factor2string()` and `step_YeoJohnson()`, these two steps store the incoming variable names in different ways.

``` r
library(recipes)

data(Sacramento, package = "modeldata")

rec <- recipe(~ city + zip + beds, data = Sacramento) |>
  step_factor2string(city) |>
  step_YeoJohnson(beds)

rec_prepped <- prep(rec, strings_as_factors = FALSE)
```

`step_factor2string()` has the names in `$columns`, where on the other  hand `step_YeoJohnson()` uses the names of its `$lambdas`.

``` r
rec_prepped$steps[[1]]$columns
#>   city 
#> "city"

rec_prepped$steps[[2]]$columns
#> NULL
rec_prepped$steps[[2]]$lambdas |> names()
#> [1] "beds"
```

This means that it can be quite hard for the user to figure out which variables are selected for a given step. Especially if filtering or other transformations are happening. We also almost no where keep the information of the names of the columns that come out. These are typically identical to the input, but in cases like `step_dummy()` and `step_pca()` they are different.

The proposed solution is the pair of functions `recipes_get_features_in()` and `recipes_get_features_out()` (names are up for debate). These S3 functions will have `recipe` and `step` methods to allow for the use cases we need.

``` r
recipes_get_features_in(rec_prepped$steps[[1]])
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   step               columns
#>   <chr>              <chr>  
#> 1 step_factor2string city
recipes_get_features_in(rec_prepped$steps[[2]])
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   step            columns
#>   <chr>           <chr>  
#> 1 step_YeoJohnson beds

recipes_get_features_in(rec_prepped)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   step               columns
#>   <chr>              <chr>  
#> 1 step_factor2string city   
#> 2 step_YeoJohnson    beds
```

These functions really shine in with more advanced recipes such as the one below, where it is virtually impossible to infer the result without running or digging REAL deep.

``` r
library(recipes)

data(ames, package = "modeldata")

ames_rec <- recipe(~., data = ames) |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_nzv(all_predictors()) |>
  step_pca(all_predictors()) |>
  prep()


# Only implemented for step_pca()
recipes_get_features_in(ames_rec$steps[[3]])
#> # A tibble: 100 × 2
#>    step     columns       
#>    <chr>    <chr>         
#>  1 step_pca Lot_Frontage  
#>  2 step_pca Lot_Area      
#>  3 step_pca Year_Built    
#>  4 step_pca Year_Remod_Add
#>  5 step_pca Mas_Vnr_Area  
#>  6 step_pca BsmtFin_SF_1  
#>  7 step_pca Bsmt_Unf_SF   
#>  8 step_pca Total_Bsmt_SF 
#>  9 step_pca First_Flr_SF  
#> 10 step_pca Second_Flr_SF 
#> # ℹ 90 more rows
```

we can use `recipes_get_features_in()` in our `bake.*()` methods for a consistent interface to get `col_names`.

title: add infrastructure section to all step test files
description:
This PR is part of https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/issues/1130.

This PR seems like it is doing a lot, but it is just moving tests around. Looking at it commit by commit is very helpful.

I'm defining infrastructure tests as tests that should be used on all steps, or all applicable tests. All steps should test that they print correctly, and all steps that uses `check_name()` should test that they are used. These are infrastructure tests.

Tests under the infrastructure section should be in alphabetical order, for no other reason than to avoid confusion when new tests are added

- Each `step_*()` and `check_*()` file gets an `# Infrastructure ----------` section in their test file.
- renamed `test-factors2string.R` to match name of step
- split `mutate()` and `rename()` tests into 2 each to the `_at()` variants have their own files.

Moved over tests that should be called for each step

description:
This is another refactor/standardize PR

I noticed that we are using every method under the sun to pull out a single column from a data.frame. This PR aims to only use `[[` for consistency.

Not that it matters hugely, but this also provides the smallest of speedups

``` r

bench::mark(
  mtcars[, col_name, drop = TRUE],
  getElement(mtcars, col_name),

)
```

title: speed up `recipes_eval_select()`
description:
I've been doing some profiling with stacks to help get a different angle on where we come across slowdowns, and ended up finding that we spend a good bit of time in `recipes_eval_select()` machinery. This PR speeds up the join and writes out the `nest()` call in `recipes_eval_select()`!

With `main` dev:

``` r
library(recipes)
library(rlang)
data(scat, package = "modeldata")

rec <- recipe(Species ~ ., data = scat)

info <- summary(rec)

quos <- quos(all_numeric_predictors(), where(is.factor))

bench::mark(
  old = recipes_eval_select(quos, scat, info)
)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   expression      min   median `itr/sec` mem_alloc `gc/sec`
#>   <bch:expr> <bch:tm> <bch:tm>     <dbl> <bch:byt>    <dbl>
#> 1 old          3.42ms   3.53ms      274.     3.4MB     6.23
```

With this PR:

``` r
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   expression      min   median `itr/sec` mem_alloc `gc/sec`
#>   <bch:expr> <bch:tm> <bch:tm>     <dbl> <bch:byt>    <dbl>
#> 1 new          1.69ms   1.74ms      558.    1.96MB     37.0
```


This does quite a bit for `prep()` times! With `main` dev:

``` r
rec <- 
  recipe(Species ~ ., data = scat) %>%
  step_impute_mean(all_numeric_predictors()) %>%
  step_impute_mode(all_nominal_predictors()) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) %>%
  step_zv(all_predictors())

bench::mark(
  old = prep(rec)
)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   expression      min   median `itr/sec` mem_alloc `gc/sec`
#>   <bch:expr> <bch:tm> <bch:tm>     <dbl> <bch:byt>    <dbl>
#> 1 new          40.6ms   41.2ms      23.4    8.75MB     11.7
```

With this PR:

``` r
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   expression      min   median `itr/sec` mem_alloc `gc/sec`
#>   <bch:expr> <bch:tm> <bch:tm>     <dbl> <bch:byt>    <dbl>
#> 1 new            31ms   31.3ms      31.6    7.92MB     10.5
```

title: Document tunable arguments
description:
This PR is a work in process to list tunable arguments of recipes. Currently it is quite hard to figure out what steps are tunable just by reading the documentation. This PR takes a stab fixing that

This PR has enough to review, and once we are happy with it, then I'll add the documentation for the remaining steps.

We are using `@includeRmd` and creating one `.Rmd` file for each step that has tunable parameters. It feels a little overkill, but I wasn't able to do it directly in the function documentation with using `.Rmd` and without creating an internal function.

The update of this approach is that we can add some step-specific information in this section. Like in the `step_pca()` case, we should properly remind the user that they shouldn't try to tune both `num_comp` and `threshold` since `threshold` trumps `num_comp`.

Some of these rules may not be completely satisfied in the package itself, and should be fixed once this PR is merged.

title: Make sure all tunable.step_*() are specified correctly
description:
When answering https://stackoverflow.com/questions/75618633/is-this-a-bug-in-tidy-models and fixing the issue in https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/pull/1100. I realized we are not testing this part of the code.

More specifically the output generated by `tunable.step_*()` is not tested to work, just that it has the right format. This results in 2 types of problems

- custom ranges are of invalid types https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/pull/1100
- calls to dials functions that either doesn't exist or were renamed

This PR aims to fix that.

description:
this PR switches out the internal helper function `is_formula()` with `rlang::is_formula()`. It is a small complexity reducing PR

It also comes with the tiniest of performance improvements

``` r
library(recipes)
library(rlang)

formula <- ~5

bench::mark(
```

title: Make step_range() backwards compatible with clipping argument

``` r
library(recipes)

data(biomass, package = "modeldata")

)

  step_range(carbon, hydrogen)
```

title: outside argument for step_percentile
description:
This PR is here to make this problem easier to handle https://community.rstudio.com/t/step-percentile-new-data-outside-range-of-training-data/156694. now you have a way to determine how values outside the range in `step_percentile()` is handled

``` r
library(dplyr)
library(recipes)

train_df <- tibble(
  a = 1:10,
  b = 10:1
)

new_df <- tibble(a = c(1, 4, 5), b = c(0.99, 5, 10.01))

# Defaults to `outside = "none"`
train_df %>%
  recipe(a ~ b) %>%
  step_percentile(b, outside = "none") %>%
  prep() %>%
  bake(new_data = new_df)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>        b     a
#>    <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 NA         1
#> 2  0.444     4
#> 3 NA         5

train_df %>%
  recipe(a ~ b) %>%
  step_percentile(b, outside = "both") %>%
  prep() %>%
  bake(new_data = new_df)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>       b     a
#>   <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 0         1
#> 2 0.444     4
#> 3 1         5

train_df %>%
  recipe(a ~ b) %>%
  step_percentile(b, outside = "lower") %>%
  prep() %>%
  bake(new_data = new_df)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>        b     a
#>    <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1  0         1
#> 2  0.444     4
#> 3 NA         5

train_df %>%
  recipe(a ~ b) %>%
  step_percentile(b, outside = "upper") %>%
  prep() %>%
  bake(new_data = new_df)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>        b     a
#>    <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 NA         1
```

title: Use cli for printing
description:
This PR should close https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/issues/426.

The printing is staying pretty close to its original format, but used {cli} under the hood.

The input section is formatted in such a way that `outcome`, `predictor` and `case_weights` always comes first. `undeclared roles` are always last, and the remaining roles are sorted according to usage.

One thing we tried to do was having the printing method being able to say `all steps are trained` but `print.recipe()` doesn't have a way to send information to `print_step()`. (this could change is future PRs) 

I also would have liked if the steps would be able to do multiple lines, but the math will be a lot harder to make that work.
Lastly, I would love if we could pass through an option to allow for printing of ALL variables. could be done by having `if(width == Inf)` since `width()` doesn't do anything right now

```r
library(tidymodels)

ames <- ames |>
  mutate(caseweight = frequency_weights(sample(c(2, 1), n(), TRUE)))

ames$Mas_Vnr_Area[1:10] <- NA

rec <- recipe(ames) |>
  update_role(Neighborhood, Overall_Cond, Exter_Cond, Exterior_2nd, Mas_Vnr_Type, Lot_Area) |>
  update_role(Sale_Price, new_role = "outcome") |>
  update_role(Roof_Matl, new_role = "ID") |>
  step_nzv(all_predictors()) |>
  step_unknown(Neighborhood, Overall_Cond, Exter_Cond, Exterior_2nd, Mas_Vnr_Type) |>
  step_geodist(lat = Latitude, lon = Longitude, ref_lat = 38, ref_lon = -77) |>
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) |>
  step_zv(all_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(starts_with("Neighborhood"))

rec
```

title: Fixes for dev dplyr
description:
This PR makes your package compatible with the next version of dplyr:

- `rename_with()` now checks that the result of the function is the right length. `paste0()` has bad recycling behavior when there are length 0 inputs so we typically use a `vec_paste0()` helper for this instead
- `slice()` with no inputs now drops all rows. We were testing this but i dont think we should test this edge case dplyr behavior so i just removed the test
- I also fixed a dev tidyr issue where we now assert that tidyselection in `drop_na()` shouldn't rename (because that isn't meaningful). And I used the more appropriate `all_of()` selector.

We plan to submit dplyr 1.1.0 on January 27th.

This should be compatible with both dev and CRAN dplyr. It would help us out if you could go ahead and send a patch version of your package to CRAN ahead of time! Thanks!

title: Indicate which step caused the error
description:
To close #420. Errors in `prep()` and `bake()` will now indicate which step caused the error. This is a pretty minimal code change, with many snapshot updates

# Before

``` r
library(recipes)

data("ames", package = "modeldata")

recipe(~., data = ames) |>
  step_novel(Neighborhood, new_level = "Gilbert") |>
  prep()
#> Error in `prep()`:
#> ! Columns already contain the new level: Neighborhood
```

# This PR

``` r
library(recipes)

data("ames", package = "modeldata")

recipe(~., data = ames) |>
  step_novel(Neighborhood, new_level = "Gilbert") |>
  prep()
#> Error in `step_novel()`:
#> ! Problem while executing step.
#> Caused by error in `prep()`:
#> ! Columns already contain the new level: Neighborhood
```

title: Avoid `map2()` when `wts` aren't used
description:
This is a small bug exposed by purrr 1.0.0 (the dev version). If you install the dev version of purrr and run the tests, then some of the `step_dummy_extract()` ones break because purrr now applies tidyverse recycling rules to its inputs in `map2()` and `pmap()`. The error looks like:

```r
> rlang::last_trace()
<error/vctrs_error_incompatible_size>
Error in `purrr::map2()` at recipes/R/extract.R:173:6:
! Can't recycle `.x` (size 4) to match `.y` (size 0).
---
Backtrace:
    ▆
 1. ├─recipes::prep(dummy)
 2. └─recipes:::prep.recipe(dummy) at recipes/R/recipe.R:278:2
 3.   ├─recipes::prep(x$steps[[i]], training = training, info = x$term_info) at recipes/R/recipe.R:434:8
 4.   └─recipes:::prep.step_dummy_extract(...) at recipes/R/recipe.R:278:2
 5.     └─purrr::map2(lvls, as.double(wts), ~rep(.y, length(.x))) at recipes/R/extract.R:173:6
Run rlang::last_trace(drop = FALSE) to see 6 hidden frames.
```

It would be great if we could get a small recipes release out to make it easier on purrr, otherwise we are going to be forced to do a release when purrr 1.0.0 eventually goes out.

The problem happens when `wts` aren't used, i.e. `wts = NULL`. Then `as.double(wts)` returns `double()`, which isn't tidyverse recyclable against `lvls`, which is typically length >1.

title: New role selectors
description:
This PR aims to close https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/issues/942, close https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/issues/669 and helps with https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/issues/193.

It does this by expanding the role selectors we have available. 

without addressing the `*_predictors()` variants we used to have

- `all_numeric()`
- `all_nominal()`

This PR makes it so we have

- `all_numeric()`
    - `all_integer()`
    - `all_double()`
- `all_nominal()`
    - `all_ordered()`
    - `all_unordered()`
        - `all_string()`
        - `all_factor()`
- `all_logical()`
- `all_date()`
- `all_datetime()`

The structure above is to indicate that `all_numeric()` captures both integers and doubles.

I made the changes to be backwards compatible. The changes are many in a way such that the type variable in `var_info` is a list column instead of a character column.

title: added another column to the summary method
New data checks
description:
@simonpcouch added a bunch of checks for cases when a user says they don't need a particular role at bake-time but actually does:

```
library(tidymodels)
tidymodels_prefer()

data(Chicago)

Chicago <- Chicago %>% select(ridership, date, one_of(stations))

n <- nrow(Chicago)
Chicago_train <- Chicago %>% slice(1:(n - 14))
Chicago_test  <- Chicago %>% slice((n - 13):n)

needs_bake <-
  recipe(ridership ~ ., data = Chicago_train) %>%
  # Create date features
  step_date(date) %>%
  step_holiday(date) %>%
  # Change date to be an id column instead of a predictor
  update_role(date, new_role = "id") %>%
  # Create dummy variables from factor columns
  step_dummy(all_nominal()) %>%
  prep()

# Davis's check_role_requirements() picks these up
bake(needs_bake, Chicago_test %>% select(-date))
#> Error in `bake()`:
#> ! The following required columns are missing from `new_data`: "date".
#> ℹ These columns have one of the following roles, which are required at `bake()` time: "id".
#> ℹ If these roles are not required at `bake()` time, use `update_role_requirements(role = "your_role", bake = FALSE)`.

# Now we say that we don't need 'date' even though we do. check_new_data()
# catches this case
still_needs_bake <-
  needs_bake %>%
  update_role_requirements("id", bake = FALSE) %>%
  prep()

bake(still_needs_bake, Chicago_test %>% select(-date))
#> Error in `step_date()`:
#> ! The following required column is missing from `new_data` in step
#>   'date_aLcii': date.
```

title: Make discretize more consistent when supplied missing values
description:
This PR aims to close #982 .

It makes it so `discretize()` will automatically remove missing values is `keep_na = TRUE`. It further updates some existing code to use `call2()`, `modify_call()` and `eval_tidy()`.

``` r
library(modeldata)
library(recipes)
data(biomass)

biomass$carbon[1] = NA
summary(biomass$carbon)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.    NA's 
#>   14.61   44.70   47.10   48.29   49.70   97.18       1
```

title: add missing tibble conversion in prep.recipe
description:
We saw an error in https://github.com/tidymodels/extratests/actions/runs/2375665870. This error didn't have anything to do with parallel processing or themis in particular. The error surfaced because `bake.step_smote()` returns a data.frame instead of a tibble.

What happened was the changes in https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/pull/979 and https://github.com/tidymodels/themis/pull/96 was done incompletely. 

We convert to tibble after each `bake.step_*` inside `bake.recipe()`

https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/blob/77fa788b3fed542c7832fc00a8b9725a165e6a46/R/recipe.R#L580

But I forgot to add the same check after each `bake.step_*` inside `prep.recipe()`. This PR fixes that.

The original goal was to make `step_normalize()` work when one variable is selected. I found that a small refactor of `bake.step_normalize()` not only fixed the issue but also provided a modest speed improvement. See below for benchmarking

# This PR

``` r
library(recipes)
library(nycflights13)

rec_spec <- recipe(~., data = flights) %>%
  step_zv(all_numeric_predictors()) %>%
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())

  rec_spec %>% prep() %>% bake(new_data = flights)
```

title: Add new step_dummy_extract
description:
This PR implements a new step that is a more advanced dummy step. Much like `step_dummy_multi_label()`. This step in essence is a short cut, that does something similar to something you could do with {textrecipes} with more effort.

```
step_tokenize() %>%
step_tokenfilter(max_tokens = threshold()) %>%
step_tf()
```

It can be used in two ways, by specifying `sep` or `pattern`. See examples below.

This will is able to make quick work of variables such as the `genres` variable we saw in [SLICED s01e08](https://www.kaggle.com/c/sliced-s01e08-KJSEks/data).

I'm not super convinced `step_dummy_regex()` is the right name.


# Examples

``` r
library(recipes)
library(modeldata)
data(tate_text)

dummies <- recipe(~ artist + medium, data = tate_text) %>%
    step_dummy_regex(artist, medium, sep = ", ") %>%
    prep()

dummy_data <- bake(dummies, new_data = NULL)

dummy_data %>%
    select(starts_with("medium")) %>%
    names()
#> [1] "medium_colour"                       
#> [2] "medium_Etching.on.paper"             
#> [3] "medium_gelatin.silver.print.on.paper"
#> [4] "medium_Lithograph.on.paper"          
#> [5] "medium_on.paper"                     
#> [6] "medium_Photograph"                   
#> [7] "medium_Screenprint.on.paper"         
#> [8] "medium_other"

# More detailed splitting
dummies_specific <- recipe(~ medium, data = tate_text) %>%
    step_dummy_regex(medium, sep = "(, )|( and )|( on )") %>%
    prep()

dummy_data_specific <- bake(dummies_specific, new_data = NULL)

dummy_data_specific %>%
    select(starts_with("medium")) %>%
    names()
#>  [1] "medium_aquatint"             "medium_canvas"              
#>  [3] "medium_colour"               "medium_Etching"             
#>  [5] "medium_gelatin.silver.print" "medium_Lithograph"          
#>  [7] "medium_on.paper"             "medium_paper"               
#>  [9] "medium_Photograph"           "medium_Screenprint"         
#> [11] "medium_other"

tidy(dummies, number = 1)
#> # A tibble: 7 × 3
#>   terms  columns                       id               
#>   <chr>  <chr>                         <chr>            
#> 1 medium colour                        dummy_regex_2rAXF
#> 2 medium Etching on paper              dummy_regex_2rAXF
#> 3 medium gelatin silver print on paper dummy_regex_2rAXF
#> 4 medium Lithograph on paper           dummy_regex_2rAXF
#> 5 medium on paper                      dummy_regex_2rAXF
#> 6 medium Photograph                    dummy_regex_2rAXF
#> 7 medium Screenprint on paper          dummy_regex_2rAXF
tidy(dummies_specific, number = 1)
#> # A tibble: 10 × 3
#>    terms  columns              id               
#>    <chr>  <chr>                <chr>            
#>  1 medium aquatint             dummy_regex_9wqh0
#>  2 medium canvas               dummy_regex_9wqh0
#>  3 medium colour               dummy_regex_9wqh0
#>  4 medium Etching              dummy_regex_9wqh0
#>  5 medium gelatin silver print dummy_regex_9wqh0
```

title: WIP: Allow for sparse matrices to be carried around inside recipes
description:
This is still a working PR, right now it just shows a proof of concept.

`step_texthash()` has been changed to return lists of sparse matrices in the sparse-column branch of textrecipes https://github.com/tidymodels/textrecipes/tree/sparse-column.

The most significant change is here
https://github.com/tidymodels/textrecipes/commit/1eadad180b868d087cef295550b252e7a7f95a17#diff-7bba23a3635537bd6ce36b00d22c7851R202-R203
where the sparse matrix is turned into a list of row-wise sparse matrices.

This PR has changes to `convert_matrix()` such that `bake()` works with `composition = "dgCMatrix"` and `composition = "matrix"` only.

``` r
#remotes::install_github("tidymodels/textrecipes", ref = "sparse-column")
library(recipes)
library(textrecipes)
library(modeldata)
data(okc_text)

okc_text2 <- okc_text %>%
  mutate(x = 1)

okc_rec <- recipe(~ essay0 + essay1 + x, data = okc_text2) %>%
  step_tokenize(essay0, essay1) %>%
  step_texthash(essay0, essay1, num_terms = 4) %>%
  prep()

juice(okc_rec)
#> # A tibble: 750 x 3
#>    essay0     essay1         x
#>    <list>     <list>     <dbl>
#>  1 <dgCMatrx> <dgCMatrx>     1
#>  2 <dgCMatrx> <dgCMatrx>     1
#>  3 <dgCMatrx> <dgCMatrx>     1
#>  4 <dgCMatrx> <dgCMatrx>     1
#>  5 <dgCMatrx> <dgCMatrx>     1
#>  6 <dgCMatrx> <dgCMatrx>     1
#>  7 <dgCMatrx> <dgCMatrx>     1
#>  8 <dgCMatrx> <dgCMatrx>     1
#>  9 <dgCMatrx> <dgCMatrx>     1
#> 10 <dgCMatrx> <dgCMatrx>     1
#> # … with 740 more rows

bake(okc_rec, new_data = okc_text2, composition = "dgCMatrix")
#> 750 x 9 sparse Matrix of class "dgCMatrix"
#>     x                               
#> 1   1   3  -1   4   8  1  10  -1  -2
#> 2   1  -2   1  -9   2 -1   1   .   .
#> 3   1  27   2  21   7  0   .   0   2
#> 4   1  11   8   5   5  2  -2  -1  -2
#> 5   1   4  -8   1   0  .   .   2   4
...

bake(okc_rec, new_data = okc_text2, composition = "matrix")
#>     x                               
#> 1   1   3  -1   4   8  1  10  -1  -2
#> 2   1  -2   1  -9   2 -1   1   0   0
#> 3   1  27   2  21   7  0   0   0   2
#> 4   1  11   8   5   5  2  -2  -1  -2
#> 5   1   4  -8   1   0  0   0   2   4
...
```

- sparse list columns should have their own vector class so they are easily identifiable in convert_matrix()

title: Support empty selections in all recipe steps
description:
This PR adds empty selection support to all recipe steps.

---

We thought that the best way to do this was to return early from each step, returning an alternate `step_empty_selection()` step, but this was problematic for a few reasons:
- We lose the column structure when you `tidy()` that step in the recipe, because the empty selection step doesn't know what columns should be there
- If you prep a recipe, then reprep it with `fresh = TRUE`, things got a little complicated because ideally you'd reprep with the original step, rather than the empty selection step we inserted
- It isn't type stable (minor issue)
- It still feels like a bit of a hack

---

SO, I've gone through all of the steps, ensuring that each one supports empty selection natively. Most required minimal changes, which is great. A few notes:

- I've replaced all usage of `ellipse_check()` with `enquos()`, since now empty selections are okay. This function is exported, so I also mentioned that it is sort of deprecated now in favor of supporting empty selections directly (but I didn't officially deprecate it).
- Each step now has 3 tests associated with it related to empty selections. One tests `prep()` / `bake()`, one tests the print method, and one tests the `tidy()` method before and after prepping.
- Going through all of this fixed a number of small edge case bugs that weren't worth a NEWS bullet. In particular, our tidy methods often contained columns that were named vectors. These have all now been un-named.

* tidies up the pkgdown site so that the newly exported `recipes_eval_select()` shows up in the section for internal tools rather than at the top and removes the quadruplication of the section on selection via role

The imputation steps and the steps for up/downsampling were already in the correct stage of the deprecation process.

title: Fix formatting of bag imputation on factors
description:
There is a bug (reported to maintainer today) in `ipred::predict.classbag()` where the factor levels of the predictions may not be correct. This results in a reverse dependency breakage.

This PR

1. temporarily converts the outcome to a factor if a character column is to be imputed. The original data is untouched. 
1. casts the imputation predictions into a format consistent with raw data (factor, character, or numeric)
1. no longer casts the data to be a factor (to be consistent with `prep(rec, strings_as_factors = FALSE)`)

I also made changes to a $%&# Rmd file that is always changing because of `cli::rule()` widths and random step id's.

title: juiced and baked data have consistent column order
description:
A new function `final_vars()` determines the variable orderings. 

Some details:

 1. When running `juice()`, the resulting columns should be consistent with the  variables in `term_info$variables`. If selectors are used, the final columns  that are returned should be a subset of those.
 2. `term_info$variables` is consistent with a recipe when _no_ steps are  skipped.
 3. If a step is skipped, its effect is only seen in `bake()`. Also, if a  step is skipped, the columns names that should be returned are possibly  inconsistent with what is in `term_info$variables`. The results might be that  there are more/less/different columns between `bake()` and `juice()`.

`final_vars()` follows this logic:

 - During `juice()` it determines which if the selected columns are consistent    with `term_info$variables` and returns them.
 - During `bake()`, the selected columns are subsetted with the names of the    processed data.

The column ordering is non-trivial. The approach here is to order the data consistent with `term_info$variables` and to add other variables at the end of the tibble. This seems reasonable but might lead to unexpected (but consistent) results.

Consider a recipe for the iris data with a single step:

```r
step_rm(Sepal.Length, skip = TRUE)
```

is used. For `juice()`, only three columns are returned. However, when `bake()` is run on the recipe, it should return all five. However, when `bake()` is run, `Sepal.Length` is not included in `term_info$variables` so this column would come at the end (instead of first as it is in `iris`).

Another odd example from the unit tests: 

``` r
library(recipes)
#> Loading required package: dplyr
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'dplyr'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     filter, lag
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'recipes'
#> The following object is masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     step

complex_ex <-
  recipe(Species ~ ., data = iris) %>%
  step_interact(terms = ~ Sepal.Length:Sepal.Width) %>%
  step_rm(Sepal.Length) %>%
  step_pca(contains("Sepal")) %>%
  step_rm(PC1, skip = TRUE) %>%
  prep()

juice(complex_ex) %>% names()
#> [1] "Petal.Length" "Petal.Width"  "Species"      "PC2"
bake(complex_ex, new_data = iris) %>% names()
#> [1] "Petal.Length" "Petal.Width"  "Species"      "PC2"          "PC1"
```

title: Improve printing of unprepped recipe steps
description:
Closes #508.

This PR switches to using `expr_deparse()` for handling printing of R expressions in `format_selectors()`. It actually has some improvements compared to just using `as.character()`, which is nice 👏 in addition to being able to correctly handle all the tidyselect functions.

Here is what using those tidyselect functions looks like now:
``` r

#> Loading required package: dplyr
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'dplyr'

example_df <- tibble(response = 1, x = 1, y = 1, z = 1)

recipe(response ~ ., data = example_df) %>% 
  step_rm(one_of(!!remove1)) %>%
  step_rm(one_of(remove2))
```

This PR reorganizes and extends the ["Ordering of Steps"](https://recipes.tidymodels.org/articles/Ordering.html) vignette, especially with regards to factor handling. Take a look and see what you think! Hopefully this can be something to point folks toward.

Especially note _where_ I put factor level handling in this sequence:

1. Impute
1. Handle factor levels
1. Individual transformations for skewness and other issues
1. Discretize (if needed and if you have no other choice) 
1. Create dummy variables
1. Create interactions
1. Normalization steps (center, scale, range, etc) 
1. Multivariate transformation (e.g. PCA, spatial sign, etc) 

Thoughts?

title: fixes for tidymodels/dials#112
description:
It turns out that using `requireNamespace()` to determine if a package is installed does not give the right value when used inside of `.onload()` (but works otherwise).

title: Register the S3 method to the class, not the full function name
description:
Closes tidymodels/tune#146

I made a typo 😭. We will need a minor recipes release for tune.

When you register a method with `s3_register()`, you supply it in the form:

`s3_register("tune::tunable", "step_knnimpute", tunable.step_knnimpute)`

I was accidentally doing:

`s3_register("tune::tunable", "tunable.step_knnimpute", tunable.step_knnimpute)`

It only fails in R devel because we currently explicitly export the tunable methods anyways, so they are "found" in the package environment during S3 lookup. This is what was changed in R devel, as noted by the NEWS entry: "S3 method lookup now by default skips the elements of the search path between the global and base environments." (i.e. any package env).

I think this change in S3 method lookup is good motivation to not explicitly export the tunable methods anyways, so we might consider also not exporting them.

title: Changes for upcoming tuning package.
description:
* `format_selector()`'s `wdth` argument has been renamed to `width` ([#250](https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/issues/250)).

* The use of `varying()` will be deprecated in favor of an upcoming function `tune()`. No changes are need in this version, but subsequent versions will work with `tune()`.

 * `format_ch_vec()` and `format_selector()` are now exported ([#250](https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/issues/250)).

 * `check_new_values` breaks `bake` if variable contains values that were not observed in the train set (contributed by Edwin Thoen)
 
 * When no outcomes are in the recipe, using `juice(object, all_outcomes()` and `bake(object, new_data, all_outcomes()` will return a tibble with zero rows and zero columns (instead of failing). ([#298](https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/issues/298)). This will also occur when the selectors select no columns. 

 * As alternatives to `step_kpca()`, two separate steps were added called `step_kpca_rbf()` and `step_kpca_poly()`. The use of `step_kpca()` will print a deprecation message that it will be going away.

 * `step_nzv()` and `step_poly()` had arguments promoted out of their `options` slot. `options` can be used in the short term but is deprecated.

 * `step_downsample()` will replace the `ratio` argument with `under_ratio` and `step_upsample()` will replace it with `over_ratio`. `ratio` still works (for now) but issues a deprecation message.

 * `step_discretize()` has arguments moved out of `options` too; the main arguments are now `num_breaks` (instead of `cuts`) and `min_unique`. Again, deprecation messages are issued with the old argument structure. 

 * Models using the `dimRed` package (`step_kpca()`, `step_isomap()`, and `step_nnmf()`) would silently fail if the projection method failed. An error is issued now. 

 * Methods were added for a future generic called `tunable()`. This outlines which parameters in a step can/could be tuned and specifies _default_ ranges for tuning (which can be over-ruled).

title: Fix rlang development warnings
description:
Closes #343 

This PR fixes a number of rlang dev warnings

Specifically:
- Use `exec()` not `invoke()`
- Use `call2()` not `lang()`
- Use `get_expr(x)` not `x[]` on a potential quosure (could also be a formula)
- Use `!!` on a single call, not `!!!` (happens in `terms_select()` with `step_interact()`. Generally we are `!!!` a list of quosures, but in some cases we just pass a single call through as `terms`)
- Use `empty_env()` rather than passing a function, `env`, to `env_parent()`

Related to #763 as a followup and continuation of that work.

I believe closes #709 but I would appreciate someone else confirming this.

title: use @family to streamline cross-references in documentation
description:
Addresses #709

This PR makes use of the `@family` tag: all functions in a family get references to the other functions in the family in the `See Also` section of the documentation. 

The families largely correspond to the grouping on the [pkgdown reference site](https://recipes.tidymodels.org/reference/index.html), however a function can belong to more than one family, e.g. `step_impute_roll()` is listed with row-wise operations but also belongs to the family of imputation steps.

Closes #708, closes  #678.

title: Fix `step_mutate()` auto naming
description:
Closes #759 

So now we can use `across()` in `step_mutate()`

The only other dplyr step that auto-named was `step_rename()`, but it makes sense there (because you need to specify the LHS and RHS of the `=` sign to specify the old and new names)

This pull request adds `step_harmonic`. `step_harmonic` generates sin and cos terms that can be used to model cyclical components. I was somewhat unclear on the optimal `tidy` (what to include) and `tunable` (tuning on period/frequency) methods so they could use a review.

They have to be documented as long as they are exported, and it makes the most sense to have them with the functions they are being replaced by.

This PR also escalates the old functions' deprecation to a warning.

description:
Closes #689 

This PR fixes the 🐛 that we have around imputing on new data that is all `NA`. Here are the new results:

``` r
#> Loading required package: dplyr
```

title: Add keep_original_cols to some more steps
description:
This PR closes #447 by adding the `keep_original_cols` argument to some more steps, allowing folks to keep (or not keep) variables used to compute features in the output of certain steps.

Unlike the steps in #635, these mostly have `keep_original_cols = TRUE` as a default to maintain their existing behavior.

This PR also has some additional documentation for steps that transform variables in place with no new names, such as `step_normalize()` and `step_cut()`, to show how to keep the original columns using `step_mutate()` or `step_mutate_at()`. It is not entirely clear or natural what new names should be in these cases and it would be a breaking or inconsistent change for us to add names for either the transformed or untransformed case, so we are _not_ going to add this option to these cases for now. We will see how users do with this as an option.

Here would be a recommended workflow using `step_mutate_at()`:

``` r
library(recipes)
#> Loading required package: dplyr
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'dplyr'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     filter, lag
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'recipes'
#> The following object is masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     step
data(biomass, package = "modeldata")

biomass_tr <- biomass[biomass$dataset == "Training",]
```

title: step_lag, step_naomit, detect_step and minor improvements
description:
This PR includes the following:

### A new function `detect_step` to determine if a particular step occurs in a recipe

Modelling functions with a default X/y interface might have arguments like do_pca_first or include_intercept. `detect_step` makes it easier to wrap these interfaces with recipes interfaces.

### `step_lag` (#37)

Using this step induces NAs in some rows, which I presume is better than dropping the rows with holes induced by lagging.

Curious if it would be good to extend so that users can subtract off a fixed `lubridate::duration` from a column of dates.

### `step_naomit`

To complement imputation methods already in recipes and make it easier for people implementing models with recipes interfaces to separate data processing and model fitting (i.e. get rid of na.rm/na.action arguments in their fit/train methods)

Since `step_naomit` operates on rows rather than columns it probably needs a different name that reflects it isn't a step. Seems like a todo for the down the road?

### Minor improvements

- Print methods for step_intercept and step_relu
- Tidy method for step_relu
- Fix bug in step_relu when specifying all_predictors as selector, and add regression test

title: Implement `contrasts` for step_dummy()
description:
I saw that you have a `contrasts` argument that does not currently work. Since you use `model.matrix()` under the hood for all of this, I've come up with an alternative way to do one hot encoding as mentioned in #120 by implementing the `contrasts` argument (this replaces the other PR I had open). By implementing it, we can take advantage of the ability to do (from [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/4560459/all-levels-of-a-factor-in-a-model-matrix-in-r)):

```
model.matrix(~ Species, iris, 
             contrasts = list(Species = contrasts(iris$Species, contrasts = FALSE)))
```

What follows are a number of examples that show off the implemented argument. The implementation mirrors how it is used in `model.matrix()`.

<details> 

``` r
library(recipes)
data(iris)

iris2 <- iris
iris2$AB <- rep(c("A", "B"), 75)

rec <- recipe(~ Species + AB, data = iris2)

# Default
rec %>%
  step_dummy(Species, AB) %>%
  prep(training = iris2) %>%
  bake(newdata = iris2)
#> # A tibble: 150 x 3
#>    Species_versicolor Species_virginica  AB_B
#>                 <dbl>             <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1                 0.                0.    0.
#>  2                 0.                0.    1.
#>  3                 0.                0.    0.
#>  4                 0.                0.    1.
#>  5                 0.                0.    0.
#>  6                 0.                0.    1.
#>  7                 0.                0.    0.
#>  8                 0.                0.    1.
#>  9                 0.                0.    0.
#> 10                 0.                0.    1.
#> # ... with 140 more rows

# Setting the contrasts option
options(contrasts = c(unordered = "contr.sum", ordered = "contr.poly"))

rec %>%
  step_dummy(Species, AB) %>%
  prep(training = iris2) %>%
  bake(newdata = iris2)
#> # A tibble: 150 x 3
#>    Species_X1 Species_X2 AB_X1
#>         <dbl>      <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1         1.         0.    1.
#>  2         1.         0.   -1.
#>  3         1.         0.    1.
#>  4         1.         0.   -1.
#>  5         1.         0.    1.
#>  6         1.         0.   -1.
#>  7         1.         0.    1.
#>  8         1.         0.   -1.
#>  9         1.         0.    1.
#> 10         1.         0.   -1.
#> # ... with 140 more rows

options(contrasts = c(unordered = "contr.treatment", ordered = "contr.poly"))

# Setting the contrast option through the contrast arugment
rec %>%
  step_dummy(Species, AB, contrast = list(Species = "contr.sum")) %>%
  prep(training = iris2) %>%
  bake(newdata = iris2)
#> # A tibble: 150 x 3
#>    Species_X1 Species_X2  AB_B
#>         <dbl>      <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1         1.         0.    0.
#>  2         1.         0.    1.
#>  3         1.         0.    0.
#>  4         1.         0.    1.
#>  5         1.         0.    0.
#>  6         1.         0.    1.
#>  7         1.         0.    0.
#>  8         1.         0.    1.
#>  9         1.         0.    0.
#> 10         1.         0.    1.
#> # ... with 140 more rows

# Using a numeric matrix - One Hot!
species_contrast <- list(Species = contrasts(iris$Species, contrasts = FALSE))

rec %>%
  step_dummy(Species, AB, contrast = species_contrast) %>%
  prep(training = iris2) %>%
  bake(newdata = iris2)
#> # A tibble: 150 x 4
#>    Species_setosa Species_versicolor Species_virginica  AB_B
#>             <dbl>              <dbl>             <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1             1.                 0.                0.    0.
#>  2             1.                 0.                0.    1.
#>  3             1.                 0.                0.    0.
#>  4             1.                 0.                0.    1.
#>  5             1.                 0.                0.    0.
#>  6             1.                 0.                0.    1.
#>  7             1.                 0.                0.    0.
#>  8             1.                 0.                0.    1.
#>  9             1.                 0.                0.    0.
#> 10             1.                 0.                0.    1.
#> # ... with 140 more rows

# Using a numeric matrix for both
species_AB_contrast <- list(Species = contrasts(iris2$Species,    contrasts = FALSE),
                            AB      = contrasts(factor(iris2$AB), contrasts = FALSE))

rec %>%
  step_dummy(Species, AB, contrast = species_AB_contrast) %>%
  prep(training = iris2) %>%
  bake(newdata = iris2)
#> # A tibble: 150 x 5
#>    Species_setosa Species_versicolor Species_virginica  AB_A  AB_B
#>             <dbl>              <dbl>             <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#>  1             1.                 0.                0.    1.    0.
#>  2             1.                 0.                0.    0.    1.
#>  3             1.                 0.                0.    1.    0.
#>  4             1.                 0.                0.    0.    1.
#>  5             1.                 0.                0.    1.    0.
#>  6             1.                 0.                0.    0.    1.
#>  7             1.                 0.                0.    1.    0.
#>  8             1.                 0.                0.    0.    1.
#>  9             1.                 0.                0.    1.    0.
#> 10             1.                 0.                0.    0.    1.
#> # ... with 140 more rows
```

</details>

title: Add one hot encoding for step_dummy()
description:
Based on #120. I'm not the expert on the formula interface, but based on this [StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/24142576/one-hot-encoding-in-r-categorical-to-dummy-variables) answer, my proposed solution seems to be an accepted way to create one-hot encoding, i.e. using `~ Species - 1`.

Because it was so similar to `step_dummy()`, I thought it would be more natural to add it as an option, rather than create a new `step_one_hot()`. Feel free to tweak as needed or throw out altogether. 

``` r
library(recipes)

recipe(~ Sepal.Width + Species, data = iris) %>%
  step_dummy(Species) %>%
  prep(training = iris) %>%
  bake(newdata = iris)
#> # A tibble: 150 x 3
#>    Sepal.Width Species_versicolor Species_virginica
#>          <dbl>              <dbl>             <dbl>
```

title: Fix/issue 206
description:
@topepo you mentioned that we could not use `as.matrix()` because of factors, but when `composition = "matrix"` is used, it is enforced that all columns are already numeric (taken care of by `step_dummy()` or something). So we should be fine.

The only difference between `as.matrix()` and `model.matrix(~ . + 0)` is then that the latter keeps the default row names of the data frame (integers 1, 2, 3) and adds them to the matrix, but `as.matrix()` does not keep them. Both keep row names if the user had supplied them to the data frame. I like this behavior better personally.

title: Throw error with name collision

``` r
library(recipes)

data <- USArrests %>%
  mutate(PC1 = "collusion")  

rec <- recipe( ~ ., data = data)
pca_trans <- rec %>%
  step_center(all_numeric()) %>%

pca_estimates <- prep(pca_trans, training = data)
#> Error: Name collision occured in `step_pca()`. The following variable names already exists: PC1.
```

title: Feature) Multiple roles, Issue 221
description:
This PR adds support for multiple roles (and types) for a single variable. Main changes are:

* `add_role()` now only adds _new_ roles for existing variables to the recipe. I think this is more in line with its name too.
* `update_role()` alters an existing role with a new role name. If multiple roles are present for a single variable, it updates all of them to the `new_role` unless the user specifies `old_role`, in which case it will only alter that one.
* The internals of `current_info()` has changed a bit so that it holds `vars` (same as before) and `data` which is a list the same length as `vars` of tibbles containing the type/role information for each variable. This is a good way to compactly store multiple roles for a single variable. It was also motivated by `tidyselect` requiring that the input vars must be unique, which this format supplies.

This allows for a couple cool things, one of which is shown below. Note that `all_predictors()` would have selected `Sepal.Width` and `Petal.Length`, but the secondary role prevented that.

``` r
library(recipes)
recipe(Species ~ ., iris) %>%
  add_role(Sepal.Width, Petal.Length, new_role = "dontcenterme") %>%
  step_center(all_predictors(), -has_role("dontcenterme")) %>%
  prep(training = iris, retain = TRUE) %>%
  juice
#> # A tibble: 150 x 5
#>    Sepal.Length Sepal.Width Petal.Length Petal.Width Species
#>           <dbl>       <dbl>        <dbl>       <dbl> <fct>  
#>  1       -0.743         3.5          1.4      -0.999 setosa 
#>  2       -0.943         3            1.4      -0.999 setosa 
#>  3       -1.14          3.2          1.3      -0.999 setosa 
#>  4       -1.24          3.1          1.5      -0.999 setosa 
#>  5       -0.843         3.6          1.4      -0.999 setosa 
#>  6       -0.443         3.9          1.7      -0.799 setosa 
#>  7       -1.24          3.4          1.4      -0.899 setosa 
#>  8       -0.843         3.4          1.5      -0.999 setosa 
#>  9       -1.44          2.9          1.4      -0.999 setosa 
#> 10       -0.943         3.1          1.5      -1.10  setosa 
#> # ... with 140 more rows
```

I've added as many tests as I can think of, but if you have any ideas on more ways to try and confuse this I'd like to hear them!

Closes #221

* Previously, if `step_other()` did _not_ collapse any levels, it would still add an "other" level to the factor. This would lump new factor levels into "other" when data were baked (as `step_novel()` does). This no longer occurs since it was inconsistent with `?step_other`, which said that 

 > "If no pooling is done the data are unmodified".

*  `step_other()` is now tolerant to cases where that step's selectors do not capture any columns. In this case, no modifications to the data are made. ([#290](https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/issues/290), [#348](https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/issues/348))

* `step_other()`'s print method only reports the variables with collapsed levels (as opposed to any column that was _tested_ to see if it needed collapsing). ([#338](https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/issues/338))
